overview: Host Danielle Balocca interviewed resident and attorney Micah-Shalom Kesselman regarding the legal status of Medford's divestment ordinance and upcoming primary elections. The discussion focused on a resident-led legal intervention to defend the city's investment policy and concerns over local ICE activity.

items.title: Favorite Local Eatery and Venue
items.summary: Kesselman recommended Deep Cuts for its chickpea sandwich and its role as a prominent venue for folk punk musicians.

items.title: Update on Values-Aligned Local Investing Ordinance Litigation
items.summary: Kesselman detailed a federal lawsuit filed against the city by the National Jewish Advocacy Center following the City Council's override of the Mayor's veto on the divestment ordinance.

items.title: Resident Intervention in Federal Lawsuit
items.summary: Twelve Medford residents filed to intervene in the litigation to provide an adequate defense of the ordinance after the city administration stated in court filings that it had no plans to enforce the law.

items.title: Discussion on Zionism and Anti-Semitism
items.summary: Kesselman discussed his letter to 'Got to Know Medford' arguing that Jewish identity should be decoupled from Zionism to prevent the use of anti-Semitic tropes in political discourse.

items.title: Medford for Palestine Political Endorsements
items.summary: The group endorsed Erika Eiderhoven for State Senate, Paul Russo for State Representative, and Jonathan Paz for the Federal House of Representatives.

items.title: ICE Activity at Mystic Avenue Courthouse
items.summary: Kesselman reported an unprecedented uptick in arrests by ICE at the local district courthouse and urged residents to engage with the immigrant rights group Luce.
